## Two valid ways to start {#method-choice}

Solve $3(x-2)+6=-27$. Expanding works; dividing both sides first can also simplify the equation.

:::::: {.example-pair}
::::: {.model}

<h3>Expand first</h3>

$3(x-2)+6=-27$

::: {.fragment}

[Expand the bracket.]{.annotation}

$3x-6+6=-27$

:::
::: {.fragment}

[Collect like terms.]{.annotation}

$3x=-27$

:::
::: {.fragment}

[Divide both sides by $3$.]{.annotation}

$\dfrac{3x}{3}=\dfrac{-27}{3}$

:::
::: {.fragment}

$x=-9$

:::
:::::
::::: {.paper}
::: {.fragment}

<h3>Divide every term by $3$ first</h3>

$3(x-2)+6=-27$

:::
::: {.fragment}

[Divide the whole of each side.]{.annotation}

$\dfrac{3(x-2)}{3}+\dfrac{6}{3}=\dfrac{-27}{3}$

:::
::: {.fragment}

[Simplify each quotient.]{.annotation}

$(x-2)+2=-9$

:::
::: {.fragment}

[Collect like terms.]{.annotation}

$x=-9$

:::
:::::
::::::

::: {.fragment}

**Both methods preserve equality.** Dividing first means dividing **every term** by $3$, including the $+6$.

:::
